title: Monocular Depth Estimation: A Survey
relevance_assessment: The paper is directly relevant as it provides a comprehensive survey of monocular depth estimation methods up to 2023, covering model architectures, training paradigms, datasets, and evaluation metrics, which aligns with the task of reviewing developments from 2023‑2025.
key_findings: Transformer‑based models (e.g., DPT, MiDaS‑v3) have become the dominant architecture, achieving state‑of‑the‑art performance on diverse benchmarks.
Self‑supervised learning from video or stereo pairs enables depth prediction without dense ground‑truth, broadening applicability to in‑the‑wild data.
Multi‑task training (depth + semantic segmentation or surface normals) improves robustness and generalization across domains.
Domain‑generalization techniques such as style randomization, feature alignment, and test‑time adaptation reduce performance drops when models are deployed on unseen environments.
limitations: Most surveys, including this one, primarily cover works published up to early 2023, so emerging 2024‑2025 methods are not exhaustively represented.
Quantitative comparisons are often limited to a few standard datasets (KITTI, NYU‑Depth V2), overlooking newer benchmarks like TartanAir or Waymo Open Dataset.
The survey notes a gap in real‑time rendering‑aware depth estimators that balance accuracy with low latency on edge devices.
evidence_snippets: “Transformer‑based architectures such as DPT and MiDaS‑v3 have set new performance records on KITTI and NYU‑Depth V2, largely due to their global context modeling.”
“Self‑supervised methods that exploit video sequences or stereo pairs eliminate the need for dense depth labels, enabling training on massive uncurated datasets.”
“Multi‑task learning frameworks jointly predict depth, semantics, and surface normals, leading to improved depth quality and better scene understanding.”
“Domain‑generalization strategies, including style randomization and feature‑level alignment, are highlighted as essential for deploying models in unseen environments.”
“The survey acknowledges that most evaluated methods are benchmark‑centric and that real‑time, edge‑friendly depth estimation remains an open challenge.”
summary: The survey provides a thorough overview of monocular depth estimation advancements up to 2023, emphasizing the shift toward transformer‑based backbones, the rise of self‑supervised learning, and the benefits of multi‑task training for robustness. It highlights domain‑generalization techniques as crucial for real‑world deployment and points out current gaps, notably the scarcity of real‑time, edge‑optimized models and limited evaluation on newer, large‑scale benchmarks. These insights establish a solid baseline for tracking the rapid progress anticipated between 2023 and 2025.
